gen_risks.description: Delay to Final Investment Decision and commercial operation due to alignment with spurline timelines.
gen_risks.mitigation: Incorporate schedule buffers, accelerate early procurement, and monitor critical path milestones closely.
gen_risks.evidence: Option 2: FID delayed by 4 months, resulting in a subsequent 5‑month delay to COD.

gen_risks.description: Revenue shortfall if ICC Contract performance thresholds are not met.
gen_risks.mitigation: Negotiate a minimum revenue floor and diversify income streams beyond the contract‑for‑difference mechanism.
gen_risks.evidence: ICC Contract provides revenue support per tonne of CO₂ captured, with performance thresholds and safeguards against under‑delivery.

gen_risks.description: Capital funding gap if the CCS Infrastructure Fund grant is delayed or reduced below 50% of eligible costs.
gen_risks.mitigation: Secure alternative financing arrangements and stage capital drawdowns to match grant receipt timelines.
gen_risks.evidence: CIF Grant provides upfront capital support during construction, up to 50% of Padeswood’s eligible capital costs.

gen_risks.description: Risk of project discontinuation before completion.
gen_risks.mitigation: Implement robust governance gates, regular stage‑gate reviews, and a contingency plan for re‑allocation of resources.
gen_risks.evidence: Section 5.4.2 lists a Discontinuation risk for Padeswood.

gen_risks.mitigation: Apply strict audit controls, independent financial oversight, and anti‑fraud training for all contractors.
gen_risks.evidence: Section 5.4.4 identifies Fraud as a financial risk.

gen_risks.description: Cross‑chain delivery risks arising from integration with other CCUS projects.
gen_risks.mitigation: Use the Cluster Sponsor Function to maintain an integrated risk register and coordinate mitigation actions across projects.
gen_risks.evidence: Section 5.4.6 highlights Cross‑chain and cross‑cutting risks.

gen_risks.description: Technical risk of integrating first‑of‑a‑kind CCS technology into an operational cement plant.
gen_risks.mitigation: Conduct detailed engineering design, pilot testing, and rely on independent technical assurance (e.g., WSP).
gen_risks.evidence: Padeswood will be the first at‑scale UK cement plant incorporating CCS technology; technical assurance provided by WSP.

gen_risks.description: Regulatory risk from future changes to the CCS Network Code or related legislation.
gen_risks.mitigation: Monitor legislative developments and embed change‑in‑law clauses in all commercial agreements.
gen_risks.evidence: Padeswood is compliant with the CCS Network Code and contracts include change‑in‑law clauses.

gen_risks.description: Market risk due to rising carbon prices and the introduction of the UK CBAM in 2027.
gen_risks.mitigation: Secure long‑term revenue contracts and perform scenario analysis for carbon price and CBAM impacts.
gen_risks.evidence: Rising carbon price and the UK Carbon‑Border Adjustment Mechanism (CBAM) to be introduced in 2027 affect competitiveness.

gen_risks.description: Stakeholder coordination risk among multiple oversight bodies (Ofgem, LCCC, DESNZ).
gen_risks.mitigation: Establish a clear governance framework with regular joint steering committee meetings and defined escalation paths.
gen_risks.evidence: Governance includes Ofgem, LCCC, DESNZ CGL and the DESNZ Cluster Function Team.

gen_risks.description: Insufficient utilisation of the CO₂ transport and storage network could erode value for money.
gen_risks.mitigation: Negotiate capacity‑commitment clauses with T&S operators and retain flexibility to adjust capture volumes.
gen_risks.evidence: Project aims to increase T&S network utilisation, supporting value for money of the HyNet cluster.

gen_risks.description: Cost overruns driven by inflation and energy price assumptions.
gen_risks.mitigation: Include escalation clauses, conduct regular cost reviews, and apply conservative inflation buffers in budgeting.
gen_risks.evidence: Cost assessment templates incorporate inflation and energy assumptions for the project.

gen_risks.description: Future reduction in subsidy support could jeopardise commercial viability after early deployment phases.
gen_risks.mitigation: Develop a pathway to profitability without subsidies and stage de‑risking milestones.
gen_risks.evidence: Future market phases are expected to operate with reduced subsidy support through competitive allocation rounds.

gen_risks.description: Organisational risk of inadequate oversight of cross‑chain delivery and post‑FID activities.
gen_risks.mitigation: Empower the Cluster Sponsor Function with clear authority and performance metrics for post‑FID monitoring.
gen_risks.evidence: Cluster Sponsor Function manages cross‑chain delivery risks and provides oversight post‑FID.

gen_risks.description: Insufficient private sector investment leading to reliance on public funding.
gen_risks.mitigation: Offer de‑risking mechanisms, transparent contracts, and clear return‑on‑investment signals to attract investors.
gen_risks.evidence: Business model aims to stimulate private sector investment by reducing investor risk.

gen_risks.description: Failure to meet CO₂ capture performance targets, affecting revenue support payments.
gen_risks.mitigation: Implement rigorous performance monitoring, LCCC contract enforcement, and contingency capture technologies.
gen_risks.evidence: Revenue support is tied to tonnes of CO₂ captured, requiring the plant to meet capture performance targets.

gen_risks.description: Data management and monitoring deficiencies could impede benefit evaluation.
gen_risks.mitigation: Adopt a comprehensive data management strategy with defined data sharing protocols and regular audits.
gen_risks.evidence: Developing a data management strategy, including reviewing relevant data sharing arrangements.

gt_risks.description: Revenue Support Agreement (RSA) risk. RSA would be paid to the T&S Company (Eni) in two circumstances: where the network is underutilised, and where users are unavailable to inject CO2 and therefore are not paying user fees. [Financial Case Sec 5.4.1, p.14-15.]
gt_risks.mitigation: Padeswood joining the T&S network will reduce the level of network underutilisation and will therefore reduce RSA payments to the T&SCo.

gt_risks.description: Discontinuation risk for Padeswood: the potential for Padeswood to be unable to continue under the business model contract due to the actions of another party or events outside its control - a large-scale, programme-wide issue (e.g. leakage), a prolonged T&S issue, or external events such as Qualifying Change in Law (QCiL), Qualifying Shutdown Events, or Force Majeure. Projects connected via a spurline can also be exposed to an additional risk if the spurline FID is taken after T&S FID, which is not within the capture project's control. [Financial Case Sec 5.4.2, p.14-15.]
gt_risks.mitigation: The risk of having to make a discontinuation payment to Padeswood is judged to be a remote contingent liability given that it is very unlikely (<1%); spurline-timing risk is treated as a variation of the existing cross-chain risks already protected by the business model.

gt_risks.description: Exchequer funding / Secretary of State direct agreement (SoSDA) risk: LCCC is only liable to make payments to the extent it has received sufficient funds from HMG, creating a risk that Padeswood would have no recourse under its private-law contract with LCCC to obtain payments owed if HMG funding to LCCC were insufficient. [Financial Case Sec 5.4.3, p.14-15.]
gt_risks.mitigation: The Secretary of State will sign a direct agreement with Padeswood (to which LCCC is also party) to fund payments directly where LCCC fails to pay; this does not increase DESNZ's overall liabilities or create a contingent liability, as it is an intragroup transaction.

gt_risks.description: Fraud risk across the CCUS programme's grant and contract payments. [Financial Case Sec 5.4.4, p.14-15.]
gt_risks.mitigation: A CCUS Fraud Management Strategy is being developed specifying the programme's strategic approach to deterrence, prevention, detection, and management of fraud and error, including counter-fraud governance and reporting structures and high-quality fraud risk assessments (FRAs) for the different tranches of the CCUS programme.

gt_risks.description: Financial sensitivities: several contractual terms are 'locked in' at Padeswood FID, but drivers of the financial impact continue to move post-FID - notably the carbon market price (Low ETS series used as the reference price for the extension period) and the opex reopener (higher opex expenditure payments), both of which could result in higher subsidy. Other financial sensitivities have the effect of reducing total subsidy. [Financial Case Sec 5.4.5, p.14-15.]
gt_risks.mitigation: Sensitivity analysis has been conducted to estimate the scale of potential subsidy increase from each driver; offsetting sensitivities are also identified and tracked.

gt_risks.description: Cross-chain and cross-cutting risks. Cross-chain risks are risks the private sector is exposed to through the network but cannot mitigate against - T&S Construction delay, Padeswood Construction Delay, Padeswood Underperformance, T&S Underperformance, and Discontinuation Provisions; Padeswood joining the HyNet cluster increases HMG's exposure to compensation payments should the T&S network fail or become unavailable. Cross-cutting risks - inflation risk, carbon price risk, and OpEx risk - are those which are challenging for the private sector to price or relate to events outside their control. [Financial Case Sec 5.4.6, p.14-15; overlaps in subject matter with the Economic Case's Sec 3.4 Risk Appraisal tables, p.10-11, which quantify the value-for-money impact of the same named risks but are a modelling input rather than a risk-register entry, and are excised from planning text for leakage safety but not scored here.]
gt_risks.mitigation: Risk allocation is designed so that each risk sits with the party best placed to manage it; the business model contracts and Network Code are structured to limit and price cross-chain exposure.
